A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KNO research work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A and B are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original KNO benchmark results, timings, ablations, and a zero-shot super-resolution example in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations and kernel, matrix-structure, and model-size experiments.

M1.justification: The KNO architecture, objectives, lifting/projection operators, kernel formulas, interpolation, quadrature, and dimension-wise factorization are retained. The additional kernel and matrix-structure experiments investigate options within the existing framework rather than introduce a new proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven benchmarks: Burgers, Beijing-Air, two Darcy problems, NS-Pipe, NS Mach 1.0, and reaction-diffusion. The Darcy zero-shot super-resolution scenario in Appendix A.1.5 also remains unchanged. New ablations vary configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Transolver and the standalone classical kernel method KM to the accuracy and timing comparisons, retaining FNO/GeoFNO and GNOT. KM covers all seven benchmarks; Transolver has no Darcy-triangle result because its implementation cannot handle the heterogeneous input/output grids.

E3.justification: v3 introduces Transolver/KM tuning procedures and additional matrix-density and NS-Pipe model-size sweeps. Table 4 changes the main NS-Pipe KNO from 171,265 to 274,561 parameters. KM training timing measures a linear-system solve rather than an epoch. Existing benchmark splits, error metrics, and stated training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Tables 11, 12, and 15 examine finite-smoothness/compact-support kernels, matrix-valued kernel density across channel widths, and NS-Pipe depth/width sensitivity. These substantially expand the architectural analyses. Earlier component-removal, quadrature, factorization, model-size, and super-resolution studies remain after renumbering.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports uncertainty for the retained GNOT NS-Pipe result: 0.47 becomes 0.47 ± 0.02. KNO's four-initialization mean and standard-error reporting practice remains unchanged; neither an increased run count nor a new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive baseline and ablation results. Table 2 changes KNO's NS Mach 1.0 error from 52.602% to 48.636% and NS-Pipe from 0.588% to 0.317%, the latter with a larger model. Table 10 changes Beijing-Air GSM from 25.435% to 24.941%. New Transolver Beijing-Air entries conflict: 26.273% in Table 2 versus 41.68% in Table 8.

T1.justification: The two universal-approximation theorem statements and bounds are retained. Appendix B.2 now explicitly chooses a positive-definite interpolation kernel and identifies the Mercer eigenfunctions with that kernel, refining the finite-dimensional proof construction. Other mathematical edits mainly standardize notation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains geometrically flexible, parameter-efficient KNO learning. The introduction extends comparative claims to Transolver, including faster training and inference even on three-dimensional problems; v2 makes that speed claim only against GNOT.

C2.justification: v3 adds noise-based explanations for GSM's advantage and simplicity/sparsity interpretations of KM and Wendland results. It explicitly defers approximation-rate and sampling results. Section 4.2 also replaces v2's caution about parameter savings not directly yielding speed gains with a claim of gains over GNOT/Transolver, requiring qualifications from the timing tables.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2.2 adds Transolver code access and search ranges for layers, embeddings, heads, and slices, plus KM kernel choices and manual scale tuning. Existing KNO initialization, quadrature details, hardware, and baseline implementation information are largely retained.

R1.justification: The introduction and related-work discussion substantially expand coverage of early PDE surrogates, PDE-Net, BCR-Net, GIT-Net, PINO, and memory-focused research. v3 develops explicit distinctions between direct kernel learning and transform learning, and positions physics-informed training as complementary to KNO.

P1.justification: Sections 1 and 1.1 are extensively rewritten and expanded. Former Sections 2.2–2.5 become subsections under a new Discretization section with an explanatory roadmap. The conclusion is expanded and acknowledgements are added, producing substantial narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two-column to single-column formatting with different typography and display placement. v3 adds architecture and discretization schematics, three ablation tables, and comparator columns in existing tables. Earlier scientific figures remain, resized or relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Added baselines, targeted ablations, broader research context, and method schematics strengthen the paper. However, v3 introduces conflicting Transolver Beijing-Air errors in Tables 2 and 8 and extends speed-superiority claims to Transolver despite Tables 5–6 showing KNO slower on reaction-diffusion. These problems affect central accuracy and efficiency comparisons. The benefits and reporting harms do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
